candidates.exact_span: A description of how the pathogen reduction requirements are met (including site restrictions for Class B sludge, if applicable).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether pathogen-reduction documentation is an operative monitoring/recordkeeping obligation for a given site depends on interpreting 'if applicable' for Class B sludge and what 'met' requires; that affects which FY2025 monitoring requirements are in scope (B) and how to classify periods without supporting records (C).

candidates.exact_span: The recommended agronomic loading rate from the references listed in Section II.3.c. above, as well as the actual agronomic loading rate shall be retained.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A different reading of 'retained' versus an enforceable numeric ceiling, and of which rate (recommended vs actual) governs compliance, could change whether agronomic loading is treated as a numeric limit for comparison (A) and whether retaining those rates is itself a monitoring/recordkeeping duty (B).

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the site restrictions in 40 CFR Part 503.32(b)(5) are met for each site on which Class B bulk sewage sludge is applied.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability hinges on whether sludge is Class B bulk sewage sludge and land-applied at a given site; different interpretations of that condition change which monitoring/recordkeeping obligations attach (B) and whether absent records reflect conditional non-requirement or missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: A certification statement that all applicable requirements (specifically listed) have been met, and that the permittee understands that there are significant penalties for false certification including fine and imprisonment. See 40 CFR 503.17(a)(4)(i)(B) or 40 CFR Part 503.17(a)(5)(i)(B) as applicable to the permittees sludge treatment activities.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which requirements are 'specifically listed,' which 503.17 subsection applies 'as applicable to the permittees sludge treatment activities,' and whether certification is itself an evidence obligation all affect the set of operative monitoring duties (B) and how to treat missing certification versus missing underlying monitoring data (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the permittee supplies the sludge to another person who land applies the sludge, the permittee shall notify the land applier of the requirements for recordkeeping found i n 40 CFR 503 .17 for persons who land apply.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether sludge was supplied to a third-party land applier determines if this notification/recordkeeping duty applies and who must hold the records; different readings change which party's FY2025 monitoring obligations are evaluated (B) and where missing evidence should be attributed (C).

candidates.exact_span: The cumulative amount of each pollutant in kilograms/hectare listed in Table 2 applied to each site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This passage ties pollutant mass loading per hectare to Table 2 parameters; interpretation of whether those cumulative figures are enforceable numeric limits, required monitoring outputs, or mere recordkeeping changes limit-comparison results (A), monitoring applicability (B), and the classification of absent Table 2 loading data (C).

candidates.exact_span: The date and time sludge is applied to each site.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Application timing can gate season-, event-, or discharge-occurrence-dependent monitoring requirements; different readings of when this record is required versus when it is merely historical description change which FY2025 monitoring obligations are deemed applicable (B) and whether missing timestamps leave applicability unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: A description of how the requirements to obtain information in §503.12(e)(2) are met.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The scope of 'requirements to obtain information in §503.12(e)(2)' is external to this segment; divergent interpretations of that cross-reference change which information-gathering duties count as operative monitoring obligations (B) and whether absent descriptions indicate unmet duties or unresolved applicability (C).
